1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods — reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to recent history.

2. Forecast tends to rise too steeply after sharp price spikes — cap upward momentum at 1.5x recent peak or 3–5% above prior 7-day average.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if forecast exceeds 30% above recent 30-day mean, adjust downward by 0.5–1.0 standard deviation.

4. Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by subtracting 0.5–1.0 from the first 3–5 forecast points.

5. Model fails to capture sudden drops — if true outcome drops below 30% of prior 7-day high, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.0 standard deviations.

6. Forecast overcorrects after corrections — if true price rebounds after a drop, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 standard deviation to avoid overshoot.

7. Model ignores long-term trend — if true price exceeds 30-day moving average by >5%, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 standard deviation to align with trend.

8. Forecast exhibits “plateauing” after spikes — if forecast exceeds 30% above prior 7-day high for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 0.5–1.0 standard deviation.

9. Model underestimates volatility — if true price deviates >2.0 standard deviation from forecast, adjust forecast to match volatility of recent 30-day range.

10. Forecast overestimates near-term price — if true outcome is below forecast by >1.5 standard deviation for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 standard deviation.
